name: FL-20
label: Safe D

key_factors: Prediction markets price Democratic win near 95%
model.rationale: The D+20 district, an incumbent with $1.9 million on hand against a Republican who has raised under $65,000, and markets pricing a Democratic win at 95% all point to a safe hold. The forecast sits near the fundamentals-based baseline with a slight trim for the open-seat dynamics after the resignation.
model.watch: Any late surge in Republican spending or polling showing a single-digit race would warrant a downgrade toward Likely D.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Incumbent Debbie Wasserman Schultz (D) is running.

overview:
Debbie Wasserman Schultz defends a heavily Democratic South Florida seat in a special-context election following Sheila Cherfilus-McCormick's resignation. The district's D+20 lean gives Democrats a strong structural advantage, and the incumbent is running with the benefits of name recognition and seniority.

Resources are lopsided: Wasserman Schultz has raised about $3.3 million and holds $1.9 million on hand, while Republican Brent Andersen has raised roughly $64,000. No independent or outside spending of significance backs the challenger, no public polls are available, and prediction markets put the Democratic win probability around 95%. With no expert ratings and no polling, the forecast rests on fundamentals, which point to a comfortable Democratic hold.
